briefdescription.para: Status codes for address-range containment checks (inclusive bounds).

detaileddescription.para: Indicates whether the tested range is fully contained within a bounding range. Used as the return type of checkAddrRangeContainment().

Values:
ADDR_IN_RANGE (0x3C): The tested range is fully contained.
ADDR_RANGE_OVERLAP (0xC2): The tested range partially overlaps.
ADDR_NOT_IN_RANGE (0xC3): The tested range is not fully contained.
Note: These are non-boolean sentinels; compare explicitly with the enumerators.

inbodydescription.para: Guard against RegionAddr + RegionSize overflowing the 64-bit address space

Mem-Regn address validity and/or Subsystem level access checking
For Built-in Subsystems (PMC & ASU), there are no requirements and hence we perform only physical address range checking for all the available Mem-Regns.
For other Subsystems (Default and User-Defined), we perform both, i.e address range checking and Subsystem level access checking.
Note: PL Mem-Regn is special condition where we check PLD Power and EOS bit and conclude entire access checking (PL has no parent controller node).
Guard against zero-size mem-regn: MemSize=0 would underflow and produce an arbitrarily large address range

skip iteration to failure for memory type mismatch during overlapping condition
only access to same memory type is allowed during overlapping condition
NOTE: This assumes that no MemRegns are overlapping between subsystems. In future if MemRegns sharing is supported, then the following assumption needs to be updated accordingly.
If we encountered overlapping region(s) but didn't fully consume the range (no ADDR_IN_RANGE break), it's a failure. goto done to skip the PL power check (which would override Status).
Built-in subsystems (PMC/ASU) are trusted; a non-PL range not covered by a Mem-Regn defers to the memory-controller state check in XPm_IsMemAddressValid().

listitem.para: PL fabric has no parent controller node; reachability is decided by the PLD power domain being ON and the CFU end-of-startup asserted. Note: For any other Mem-Regn, power checking is done by retrieving their parent's controller node in XPm_IsMemAddressValid()

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a given address range (addr + size) is fully reachable through RUNNING memory-controller devices (OCM/TCM/DDR).

parameterdescription.para: 1U => emit the per-device diagnostic PmErr logs ("Node not running" and "Mismatch Memory type access!"); 0U => silent.

simplesect.para:
Status of the operation:
XPM_SUCCESS: entire range contained in RUNNING device(s)
XPM_PM_NO_ACCESS: range found but a part not RUNNING
XPM_ERR_MEM_ACCESS_TYPE: cross-type overlap
XPM_FAILURE: range not found / unresolved overlap

Shared reachability core used by XPm_IsMemAddressValid() and the memory-table State projection. The per-device diagnostic PmErr logs ("Node not running" and "Mismatch Memory type access!" - 4 in total) are gated by EnableLog: XPm_IsMemAddressValid() passes 1U to preserve its original logging, while the high-frequency State refresh passes 0U to stay silent (no log spam). Return codes are identical for both callers.

supported Mem-Regn Devices
OCM
TCM
DDR
note: PL Mem-Regn is supported but it doesn't have parent device

Save remaining chunks of region This is needed to restore chunk region for interleaved controllers
Guard against zero-size DDR region Size=0 would underflow and produce an arbitrarily large address range

skip iteration to failure for memory type mismatch during overlapping condition
only access to same memory type is allowed during overlapping condition
check power state of the given Memory Controller Device

Restore the region until it's either:
Last interleaved controller
or it's non-interleaved controller with overlap
If we encountered overlapping region(s) then: We haven't exhausted all the memory chunks of provided Region in entire iteration, hence it's a failure!

briefdescription.para: Compute whether the PL fabric is physically reachable now.

detaileddescription.para: A PL region has no parent controller node, so reachability is decided by the PL power domain being ON and the CFU end-of-startup (EOS) being asserted in hardware.

simplesect.para: 1U if the PL fabric is reachable, 0U otherwise.
